aggressive_definition_excerpt: Conditional multivariable logistic regression analysis associated analyte levels with lethal prostate cancer incidence after adjusting for body mass index and PSA.
study_design: Prospective nested case-control analysis within the PLCO Cancer Screening Trial cohort
reason: Baseline serum biomarkers were evaluated prospectively in relation to lethal prostate cancer incidence. The abstract does not report an analysis of total or general incident prostate cancer. The total analytic sample was not stated directly and was not inferred by summing cases and controls.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Relative to those in the first quartile, cases with the highest baseline levels of choline (Q4 OR: 2.19; 95% CI, 1.23-3.90; P-trend: 0.005) and betaine (Q4 OR: 1.86; 95% CI, 1.05-3.30; P-trend: 0.11) exhibited increased odds of developing lethal prostate cancer.
estimate_classifications.reason: The choline estimate explicitly concerns developing lethal prostate cancer.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Baseline serum levels of choline, carnitine, betaine, γ-butyrobetaine, crotonobetaine, phenylacetylglutamine, hippuric acid, and p-cresol sulfate were quantified and analyzed by quartile. Conditional multivariable logistic regression analysis associated analyte levels with lethal prostate cancer incidence after adjusting for body mass index and PSA.
estimate_classifications.reason: The abstract establishes carnitine as an analyte evaluated for lethal prostate cancer incidence, although the row's numerical carnitine estimate comes from supplied full-text evidence.
